newsitem.title: UK: London gold stabilising at lower levels.
newsitem.headline: London gold stabilising at lower levels.

text.p: Gold prices were easier and vulnerable to further losses on Tuesday morning following a sharp sell off in New York overnight, analysts said.
But physical buying in Asia and Europe helped stabilise the market after a brief dive to $373.00 an ounce overnight, dealers said.

"I think it's going to stabilise around here in the short term. It should hold technically in the $372-$375 area," a London-based dealer said. Bullion fixed at $374.50 an ounce, a fresh low fixing since March 2, 1995 and down nearly $1.00 from the previous fix.
Market sentiment was overwhelmingly bearish as investors shunned gold in favour of surging equities markets, and physical demand remained lower than expected.
Fears over the prospect of gold sales by miners and European central banks were also helping depress the price.
Gold was looking weak on historical price charts, and technical analysts predicted further losses.
"Selling pressure has increased, forcing prices clearly into new low ground and introducing our lower target of $372," said analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge.
Other analysts pegged gold's chief support level at $368-$370, the lows of mid-1994.
But in the near term the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday and Friday would discourage dealers from taking fresh positions this week, dealers said.
"The move in New York may have been a squaring-up of positions ahead of Thanksgiving. It's probably going to be a slow rest of the week," a dealer said.
The expiry of over-the-counter options on Wednesday might also help prices to edge up temporarily towards $375.
Silver followed gold lower overnight to a fresh 20-month low of $4.70 an ounce, but prices later bounced back.
Prices were indicated at $4.75/$4.77 an ounce, down five cents from Monday's London close.
"Silver came off without any great amount of selling. It's really following on the coat tails of gold," a dealer said, pegging the near-term price band at $4.70-$4.80.
Platinum was also lower in brisk early European business, fixing at a near three-year low of $379.00, the lowest fix since December 10, 1994.
Technical analysts said it had the potential to head towards $375 an ounce.
Palladium was also easier at $115.50/$116.50, off $1.00.
